claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi subjected to sliding in 3.5 wt% NaCl undergoes coupled tribo-corrosion degradation.
Mechanical wear removes the alloy's protective passive oxide film faster than the film can repassivate.
Wear-driven passive-film removal governs the coupled tribo-corrosion response.
Passive-film removal continuously exposes bare alloy to accelerated corrosion.
Static exposure of CoCrFeMnNi to 3.5 wt% NaCl produces an initially protective passive oxide film.
Repeated sliding prevents full repassivation of the worn surface.
Persistent bare-metal exposure accelerates localized corrosion.
The cycle of film removal, incomplete repassivation, and localized corrosion enhances total degradation.
Tribo-corrosion will produce greater total degradation than either pure wear or static corrosion.
Tribo-corrosion will increase wear volume relative to the baseline conditions.
Tribo-corrosion will elevate corrosion current density relative to static corrosion.
Elevated corrosion current density indicates reduced passive-film thickness.
Elevated corrosion current density indicates slower repassivation kinetics.
The prediction applies at room temperature in 3.5 wt% NaCl under controlled sliding at 0.1 m/s and 5 N.
Electrolyte additives or treatments that stabilize the passive film may cause the prediction to fail by enhancing repassivation.
Significantly altered wear conditions may cause the prediction to fail.

contradictions.description: The prediction and baseline require comparison with both corrosion-only and pure-wear conditions, but the falsification design specifies only static immersion and sliding in corrosive NaCl. It omits a wear-only, noncorrosive control, so the claimed comparison against pure wear cannot be tested by the stated design.
